text:
Matthew Schaefer is 19 years old and playing 27 minutes a night. That is more than two minutes up on his Calder Trophy season, and he has turned it into 15 points in 15 games. The Islanders are leaning on him like a franchise defenseman because, by the numbers, he already is one.

Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 99th percentile among defensemen last season while stuck with some of the weakest teammates in the league. This year the shots are coming in bunches (54 already), his skating ranks at the very top of the league in 20-mph bursts, and his 95.8-mph top shot is in the 94th percentile. The flag says breakout, and for once the process agrees: his team is actually finishing below its chances with him on.

Off the ice, the Islanders this week unveiled the Jennifer Schaefer Child Support Room at a Long Island cancer center, named for his mother. On it, the minutes question remains: NHL.com's Stefen Rosner has been asking why he doesn't get full power plays. We'd watch whether that changes before his ice time cracks 30 for good.
headline: Schaefer, 19, is already playing 27 minutes
